sentences.text: Smt Samta Jain - Government Advocate for the respondent
Heard on I.A.No.20070/2024, the first application under Section 430 (1) of BNSS for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to the appellant/accused 'S', pending the appeal.
Appellant/accused 'S' has been convicted for commission of offence under Sections 376 (1) of IPC and Section 3 read with Section 4 of the POCSO Act.

For the commission of offence under Section 376(1) of IPC, appellant/accused 'S' has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years & to pay fine of Rs.2000/- with default stipulation vide judgment dated 26.07.2024 passed in S.C. No.170/2022 (State of M.P. vs. Accused 'S' and another) by III rd Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Sagar (MP).

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that appellant/accused 'S' has been erroneously convicted by learned trial Court as it has not properly appreciated the evidence of prosecution witnesses and material on record.

It is submitted that evidence of prosecution witnesses is full of omissions and contradictions and such omissions and contradictions have not been considered in right perspective by the learned trial Court.
This is an appeal of 2024 and there is no possibility of hearing of this appeal in near future.
Therefore, if the execution of jail sentence of appellant/accused 'S' is not suspended, the purpose of filing this appeal would become futile.
Thus, it is prayed that custodial jail 2 CRA-9468-2024 sentence of the appellant/accused 'S' may be suspended and the appellant may be released on bail.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the appellant/accused 'S'.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the material available on record.
Appeal is of the year 2024 and there is a bleak possibility of hearing of this appeal in the near future.

Therefore, if jail sentence of the appellant is not suspended, the purpose of filing appeal would Accused S vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49278694/
1 become futile.

sentences.text: Hence, a case for suspension of jail sentence pending the appeal is made out.

Consequently, I.A.No.20070/2024 is allowed and execution of jail sentence of appellant/accused 'S'
is hereby suspended.

It is directed that subject to depositing the entire fine amount, if not already deposited appellant/accused 'S' be released on bail on appellant's furnishing a personal bond to a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the trial Court on 02.09.2025 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List this case for final hearing in due course.
